quirks.summary: Search-result metaInfo fields are separated by U+00B7, not '|', so a parser splitting on '|' swallows the whole block and every reference arrives with its metadata attached.
quirks.detail: A reference comes back as '26/01680/DOC · Received: … · Validated: …' rather than '26/01680/DOC'. That silently defeats suffix-based scoping — condition discharges pass straight through a filter keyed on the suffix. The same bug was observed at Horsham.
quirks.workaround: Split on U+00B7 (or take the reference up to the first separator) and confirm the suffix filter actually excludes something before trusting a cohort.

source_notes:
The only Sussex Idox install so far on the STANDARD document route (Recipe C): it has a real `documents` tab, where Mid Sussex, Horsham, Lewes and Adur & Worthing all use `externalDocuments` pointing at a separate store. Verified end to end 22 Aug 2026: documents tab -> /online-applications/files/{32-HEX}/pdf/{name} -> real PDF (%PDF-), Referer set to the documents-tab URL. RATE LIMIT: 429s at 3s spacing (as Horsham); 6s is stable. REFERENCES CARRY NO COUNCIL PREFIX - the form is YY/NNNNN/TYPE and the TYPE suffix is the only scope signal, so cohort rules must key on the suffix, not a prefix. SAME METADATA-SEPARATOR BUG AS HORSHAM: result metaInfo is separated by U+00B7 '.' not '|', so a parser using [^|]+ swallows the whole block and every reference arrives as '26/01680/DOC . Received: ... . Validated: ...'. That silently defeats suffix-based scoping - condition discharges pass straight through.

SCOPE TRAP: the ADJ suffix is 'adjoining authority consultation' - applications DECIDED BY ANOTHER AUTHORITY (South Downs NPA, Arun, East Hampshire, Havant) on which Chichester is only a consultee. Eight sat in a first-pass major-housing cohort; left in they attribute other councils' decisions to Chichester. Also exclude PREMP/PRESMP (pre-application enquiries), HRA (reg 77 assessments), DOM, ELD/PLD. Keep OBG (s106 obligation discharge) for triage - it is a commitment-change vehicle. Scope caveat: much of the district is in the South Downs National Park where SDNPA is the LPA, so the district's major-housing set is genuinely reduced.
